workflows.title: How to associate a control with a risk's treatment plan
workflows.purpose: From a risk's edit drawer, use the Treatment Plan section to associate one or more existing controls with that risk.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Risks
In the risk table, click the row actions menu for the target risk and click "Edit" to open the risk drawer.
In the drawer, scroll to the "Treatment Plan" section (between Inherent risk and Residual risk).
Click "Edit" in the Treatment Plan section header to enter edit mode.
Optionally type in the "Search controls" field to filter the control list.
Check the checkbox next to each control you want to associate with the risk.
Click "Save Changes" to confirm the association (or "Cancel" to discard).
Verify the associated control now appears listed under "Treatment Plan" as a clickable link to the control register.

workflows.title: How to link a test to additional entities
workflows.purpose: Link an existing compliance test to one or more of the firm's business entities so edits and completion status stay in sync across them.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests
Click a test row to open its detail page (e.g. /firm_oversight_v2/tests/[id])
Open the actions dropdown menu on the test detail page
Click "Link test to entity"
In the dialog titled "Select entities to link this test.", use the "Search entities" field to find the entity you want
Toggle the switch next to each entity you want to link — the row will show "Sync enabled" once toggled on
Click "Link" to save (button shows "Linking..." while saving)
Confirm the toast notification "Link test enabled" — "This test is now linked across different entities. Edits and completion will stay in sync."

workflows.title: How to create a new test
workflows.purpose: Set up a new compliance test through the multi-step wizard, from basics through questionnaire, scheduling, ownership, and review.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests
Click "Add test".
Enter the test title/description, pick a manual and category, then click Next.
Build or select the questionnaire template, then click Save and next.
Choose one-time or recurring schedule and set due dates, then click Next.
Assign the test owner and reviewer, then click Next.
Review the full test configuration and click Save test.

workflows.title: How to notify an employee about an expired account connection
workflows.purpose: Send a one-off email reminder prompting an employee to reconnect a broken or expired brokerage account connection from their employee detail page.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Employees
Click on the employee's name to open their employee detail page.
Select the "Accounts" tab to view the employee's connected brokerage accounts.
Locate the account showing an "Expired connection" or "Connection expired" status pill.
Click "Actions" to open the actions menu.
Click "Send email reminder" in the dropdown.
Review the "Send reminder email?" confirmation dialog, which explains the employee will be emailed to connect or reconnect their investment accounts.
Click "Send" to dispatch the reminder email.
Confirm the "Email sent" toast confirmation appears, indicating the reminder was delivered to the employee.

workflows.title: How to send continuing education reminder emails
workflows.purpose: Send bulk or per-course reminder emails to employees with incomplete continuing education courses from the Continuing education tab.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Continuing education
Click the "Courses" tab to view courses with enrolled employees.
Either select one or more courses using the row checkboxes, or click the row actions menu (⋮) on a single course and choose "Send reminder".
If courses are selected, click "Send reminders" in the bulk actions bar that appears above the table.
Review the pre-filled reminder email in the modal, including course name(s), overdue course count, and assigned course count.
Optionally select a different template using the email template selector, or edit the subject and body directly.
Click "Send" (or the modal's send action) to dispatch the reminder emails to all employees with incomplete assignments for the selected course(s).

workflows.title: How an employee completes and signs a certification
workflows.purpose: An employee opens an assigned certification task, answers all required questions, reviews the Final disclaimer, and submits their electronic signature for review.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Certifications (employee view: /employee/certifications)
Click a pending certification task in the list to open it, loading the task detail page at /employee/certification/[taskId]
Answer each required question in the questionnaire, using the progress sidebar or the footer Previous/Next navigation to move between questions
Optionally click "Save as draft" at any point to save progress and return later
Scroll to the "Final disclaimer" section at the end of the questionnaire
Check the first attestation checkbox confirming the certification responses are accurate
Check the second attestation checkbox confirming the electronic signature, with "Legal first name" and "Legal last name" shown read-only
Click "Submit" (button is disabled until all required questions and both attestation checkboxes are complete)
Confirm the "Certification submitted" toast confirmation appears, or "Certification auto-approved" if auto-approval applies
The page returns to /employee/certifications, where the task now shows as pending review (or approved)
